title: Beef and Ale Casserole
subtitle: A slow-braised British pub classic
excerpt: Beef shin braised low and slow in dark ale until the meat falls apart and the sauce turns rich and glossy. Serve with mash or dumplings and you have a proper cold-weather supper.

recipe.sourceNotes: Beef and ale casserole is a fixture of British farmhouse and pub cooking. The combination of dark ale and root vegetables for braising beef appears in regional cookery books from the nineteenth century onward.

recipeTools.notes: A heavy cast-iron pot holds heat evenly for long braising.

content.text: Beef and ale casserole is a slow braise of beef shin in dark ale with root vegetables and herbs. The long cooking softens the connective tissue in the shin, which thickens the sauce to a glossy, rich gravy that coats every piece of beef. Give it three hours and it virtually looks after itself.
Heat the oven to 160 C / fan 140 C / gas 3. Toss the beef chunks with the flour, salt, and black pepper until coated all over.
Heat the oil in a large dutch oven over a high heat. Brown the beef in two or three batches, turning to colour on all sides, about 3 minutes per batch. Lift the beef out and set aside.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until softened at the edges. Add the garlic and cook for another minute.
Stir in the tomato puree and cook for 1 minute. Pour in the ale and stock. Scrape up any browned bits from the base of the pot. Add the Worcestershire sauce, thyme, and bay leaves.
Return the beef to the pot. The liquid should come about two-thirds up the meat. Bring to a simmer, then cover with a tight-fitting lid and transfer to the oven.
Braise for 2 hours 30 minutes to 3 hours, until the beef is completely tender and the sauce has thickened. Remove the thyme stalks and bay leaves. Taste for seasoning before serving.
Sauce too thin: remove the lid for the last 30 minutes to let it reduce.
Bitter flavour from the ale: add a teaspoon of sugar or a splash of balsamic vinegar to round it out.
Beef still tough at 2 hours 30 minutes: the pieces were probably too thick or the shin was particularly dense. Give it another 30 to 45 minutes.
